_comment: Brain ontology: the object types and relations a built brain exposes, derived deterministically from a note's frontmatter (type + category + kind). No AI decides anything here. graphdata.py counts real nodes/edges against this file to emit graph.json `ontology`; Studio and the website draw from that block. First matching object wins, so specific rules (category/kind) come before generic ones. `subject` limits an object to personal or company brains; omit it for both. Relations describe the DIRECTION and human label of an existing graph.json edge type; stored edges stay undirected (retrieval parity). Override with --mappings <dir>/brain/ontology.json. Plan: second-brain-link-docs/docs-ontology/.

objects.label: Organization
objects.subject: company
objects.meaning: The company this brain is about — everything else links back here.

objects.label: Me
objects.subject: personal
objects.meaning: You — profile, roles, skills; the root of the brain.

objects.label: Person
objects.meaning: Someone in this company's world: employee, contact or partner. However many exports named them, one note.
objects.meaning_person: Someone you know. Every platform that knows them points at this one note.

objects.label: Account
objects.subject: company
objects.meaning: A customer. Its deals, contacts and documents link here.

objects.label: Team
objects.subject: company
objects.meaning: A department or group; its members link in.

objects.label: Channel
objects.subject: company
objects.meaning: A room a team talks in — who is in it, never what was said.

objects.label: Project
objects.subject: company
objects.meaning: A body of tracked work and the people on it.

objects.label: Wiki space
objects.subject: company
objects.meaning: A knowledge space and who writes in it.

objects.label: Company
objects.meaning: An organization named somewhere in your data.
objects.meaning_person: A company you worked at, follow, or know people at.

objects.label: Campaign
objects.subject: company
objects.meaning: A marketing campaign and the accounts it reached.

objects.label: Post
objects.meaning: Something published — by the company, or about it.

objects.label: Meeting
objects.meaning: Who met whom, and when — signal, not content.

objects.label: Document
objects.meaning: A file from a linked store, filed by area.

objects.label: Place
objects.meaning: A location: offices, venues, saved places.

objects.label: Market view
objects.meaning: How platforms and their algorithms see you.

objects.label: Career
objects.subject: personal
objects.meaning: Roles, applications, and the path between them.

source_objects._comment: Which objects each source can produce (pre-build: brain_structure.json ontology_suggested). A source's own subject (personal/company) follows its adapter package.
